summary: CODEC combines gradient-based hidden-unit attribution (Integrated Gradients) with sparse autoencoders trained on channel contributions rather than activations, and applies this to ResNet-50, ViT-B, and CNN models of the retina. The framework is well-motivated and yields several interesting empirical observations (increasing sparsity/dimensionality of contributions with depth, decorrelation of positive/negative effects, contribution modes better correlated with ImageNet classes than activation modes, effective targeted ablation) plus a nice cross-domain application to retinal circuit models. However, the paper's core methodological novelty is a combination of established techniques, key modern interpretability baselines (SAEs on activations at scale, path patching, causal tracing/distributed alignment) are not directly compared beyond a same-architecture SAE-on-activations control, statistical characterization is thin (few error bars, limited seed reporting), and generality claims exceed the evidence in places (e.g., ViT results acknowledged as inferior with limited exploration).
strengths: Clear conceptual motivation from neuroscience for analyzing contributions (receptive × projective field) rather than activations alone, with a well-articulated distinction from activation-based SAE interpretability.

Multi-pronged validation: correlational (class alignment of modes), causal (ablation/preservation experiments in Fig. 6), and cross-domain (retinal CNN in Fig. 8), which together are more convincing than any single line of evidence.

Interesting and non-obvious empirical findings, particularly the layerwise decorrelation of positive and negative contributions and the sharp change in ablation efficacy around blocks 6–7 of ResNet-50.

Application to biological retinal models is a genuine strength — the ability to generate experimentally testable hypotheses about combinatorial interneuron actions and dynamic receptive fields differentiates this from typical ANN-only interpretability work.
Hyperparameter robustness analyses (thresholds, dictionary size, seeds, L1) are reported in the supplement, addressing an obvious concern with SAE methods.
The InputGrad-style contribution mapping (Fig. 7) provides a concrete downstream use of the modes for human interpretation.

key_concerns.issue: Missing comparisons to modern interpretability baselines beyond same-architecture activation SAEs. There is no head-to-head comparison with recent SAE-on-activations work at comparable scale, causal tracing, path patching, DAS, or attribution-patching-based feature discovery — all of which are directly relevant baselines for both the class-correlation and ablation experiments.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add quantitative comparisons on the ablation/preservation task and class-correlation metrics against at least (a) a standard activation SAE with matched capacity, (b) an attribution-patching or path-patching baseline, and (c) simple gradient-magnitude channel selection, to isolate what the decomposition of contributions specifically buys over each.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical characterization is weak. Most quantitative claims (sparsity trends, decorrelation curves, mode-class correlations, ablation curves, retinal clustering) are reported without error bars, seed statistics, or significance tests. Robustness in Supp. Figs. S3–S4 is stated verbally rather than shown with distributions.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± s.e.m. across multiple SAE seeds for all headline plots (Figs. 3, 5, 6, 8), include statistical tests for the layerwise trends (e.g., correlation vs. depth), and provide confidence intervals on the ablation performance score in Fig. 6E.

key_concerns.issue: Generality is asserted more strongly than the evidence supports. ViT results are conceded to be 'inferior', LLM analysis is deferred to supplement/future work, and the ImageNet experiments are largely restricted to selected blocks of a single architecture (ResNet-50). The abstract and conclusion nevertheless frame CODEC as a general 'framework for understanding how nonlinear computations evolve across hierarchical layers.'
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either extend the ViT (and, if possible, a second CNN family such as ConvNeXt or EfficientNet) analysis to match the ResNet depth of evidence, or scope the generality claims in abstract/conclusion to the architectures and blocks actually evaluated.

key_concerns.issue: The contribution-target choice (top-1 logit) may bias several of the headline conclusions (sparsity, dimensionality growth, mode–class correlations) since the objective is already class-selective. It is not clear how much of the observed structure is a property of the network vs. a property of choosing a class-aligned scalar target.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Repeat the layerwise sparsity/dimensionality analysis and the mode–class correlation analysis using targets that are not class-aligned (e.g., logit entropy, sum of top-k, random class targets) and show that the qualitative findings persist; the current text only claims 'consistency' across targets without showing the comparison.

key_concerns.issue: Related work coverage is uneven: the neuroscience/retina literature is well cited, but modern mechanistic-interpretability work (dictionary learning on activations at scale, circuit discovery, activation patching families) is grouped under a single sentence about Fel et al. (2023) and generic saliency methods.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a paragraph explicitly positioning CODEC against contemporary SAE and circuit-discovery approaches, and clarify what CODEC recovers that these methods cannot.

key_concerns.issue: Two separate 'LIMITATIONS' sections appear at the end of the manuscript, one of which is generic boilerplate. Calibration language elsewhere ('state-of-the-art models of neural activity', 'unified approach to neural computation') is stronger than the results warrant.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Merge into a single, specific limitations section listing concrete failure modes observed (e.g., ViT underperformance, target-choice dependence) and tone down the general claims in the abstract and conclusion.

key_concerns.issue: Reproducibility of the SAE pipeline is under-specified in the main text (encoder architecture, initialization, batch composition, whether contributions are pre-normalized before SAE training, and how the k = N·d expansion is chosen for each layer).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide a compact algorithm box or a table of per-layer SAE hyperparameters and preprocessing steps, so a reader could reimplement without the redacted code.

key_concerns.issue: Ablation-based causal claims in Fig. 6 use channel-level (not neuron- or feature-level) intervention, which means credit is assigned at a coarse granularity that partially overlaps with what activation-based channel selection already achieves. The 'necessary and sufficient' framing is stronger than a channel-level ablation curve can support.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either add a finer-grained intervention (e.g., mode-projected activation edits) or restate the claim as a comparative efficiency result over activation-based channel selection at fixed budget.

questions_for_authors: How much of the layerwise sparsity/dimensionality and decorrelation results (Fig. 3) is driven by the specific choice of top-1 logit as the contribution target? Do the qualitative trends hold for entropy and top-k targets with matched statistics?

How does CODEC compare quantitatively (both class-correlation and ablation efficacy) against a standard activation SAE with matched dictionary size and sparsity, and against simple attribution-patching-based channel ranking, on the exact same ResNet-50 blocks?
For Fig. 6D–E, what are the error bars across SAE seeds and across the random off-target class draws? Is the sharp change between blocks 6 and 7 statistically robust or a single-seed artifact?

For the retinal application (Fig. 8), how sensitive are the identified modes and the clustering to the choice of surprisal target vs. per-cell response targets, and how do the identified pathways compare to those previously reported by Maheswaranathan et al. (2023)?

Why does ViT ablation underperform CNN ablation? Is this a limitation of treating tokens as spatial dimension, of Integrated Gradients through attention, or something more fundamental about ViT computation?

The completeness property of Integrated Gradients depends on an integration path and baseline; which baseline is used for hidden-layer IG (zero activation? mean activation?), and how sensitive are the modes and downstream conclusions to that choice?
calibration_check: The abstract- and conclusion-level claims (general framework across artificial and biological networks, state-of-the-art models, unified approach) are somewhat stronger than the evidence, which is concentrated on ResNet-50 with weaker ViT support and a single retinal model family; the more specific empirical claims about sparsity, decorrelation, and ablation efficacy are reasonably scoped but under-quantified statistically.

significance.justification: A useful shift of interpretability focus from activations to contributions, with a plausible impact on both mechanistic interpretability and computational neuroscience, though not a paradigm-changing result.

novelty.justification: The core idea (SAE on Integrated-Gradients hidden contributions) is a natural but previously under-explored combination of established techniques rather than a fundamentally new methodological primitive.

rigor.justification: Method is described coherently and validated along multiple axes, but several conclusions depend on a specific contribution target and coarse channel-level interventions that are not fully controlled.

statistical_soundness.justification: Most quantitative results lack error bars, seed statistics, or significance tests; robustness claims are stated verbally rather than shown as distributions.

calibration_honesty.justification: Method-level claims are mostly scoped, but abstract/conclusion language overreaches (general framework, unified approach) relative to the ResNet-50-dominant evidence and acknowledged ViT weakness.

clarity.justification: Overall readable and the four-stage CODEC framework is clearly laid out, though some math (contribution mapping) is dense and the anonymized text has typographical/formatting artifacts.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard structure is followed with an appropriate length, though related work is thin and two overlapping limitations sections appear at the end.

reproducibility.justification: Key hyperparameters and training budget are given, but the SAE encoder architecture, preprocessing, and per-layer settings are not fully specified in the main text; description would allow rough but not exact reproduction.

related_work.justification: Neuroscience literature is well covered, but modern mechanistic-interpretability work (SAEs at scale, circuit discovery, activation/attribution patching families) is treated superficially, weakening positioning.

figure_quality.justification: Judging from captions, the figures are well planned and directly support the specific claims (pipeline, layerwise trends, mode–class alignment, ablation/preservation, retinal IRFs, contribution maps).

breadth_generality.justification: Coverage spans CNN, ViT, and retinal CNN, but ImageNet evidence is dominated by ResNet-50 on selected blocks, ViT is acknowledged as weaker, and generality claims exceed the demonstrated scope.

overall_recommendation.justification: A borderline submission: methodologically interesting and empirically suggestive, but requires stronger baselines, better statistical characterization, and more disciplined generality claims to clear the ICLR acceptance bar.
